newsitem.title: USA: Cook County suit says bonds issued for no project.
newsitem.headline: Cook County suit says bonds issued for no project.

text.p: Cook County prosecutors have filed a civil lawsuit against a suburban Chicago park district, contending it has issued more than $600,000 of bonds over the past five years and collected taxes to repay the debt while providing no discernible recreation program.

Prosecutors seek the removal of four "purported" Dixmoor Park District commissioners and ask that it be placed under court supervision for gross mismanagement, the state's attorney's office said in a civil lawsuit filed Thursday.

The civil suit claims follow by one day criminal charges lodged against a current commissioner, two former commissioners and two construction company representatives for misappropriation of $500,000, the state's attorney's office noted.

The park district issued $400,000 of general obligation bonds in 1992 after a successful voter referendum to build a recreation center and erect playground equipment on a small parcel of land in Dixmoor, the lawsuit stated.
No center was built, the grounds have been poorly maintained and the equipment remains in a constant state of disrepair, the lawsuit contends.
The district has issued more debt in the five years since and collected hundreds of thousands of dollars in taxes to repay the bonds, the civil lawsuit added.
"Despite an abundance of public funding during this period, the Dixmoor Park District has nothing tangible to show for the money it received," the lawsuit stated.

The 21-count civil lawsuit names commissioners Bonita Wright, Kathi Jackson, Sam Johnson and Robert Lewis as defendants. It also names Bank One Wisconsin Trust Company as the escrow agent for the bond proceeds.

The lawsuit further contends that Lewis and Sam Johnson received insufficient votes to serve as commissioners and asks the court to determine whether any of the four can serve in their claimed positions.

The criminal charges were filed against Wright, former commissioners Bobby Jackson and Parnell Jackson, Oakcon Construction Co. President Gayle Occomy and A-Prime Contractors President Kevin Mattison, according to a state's attorney's office news release.
